subject: Tyska 4
title: Umwelt: vocabulary and the climate debate
sourceSummary: Vocabulary on climate and the environment along with a short text on Germany's climate target, for taking part in a social debate in German.

questions.opener: A fundamental word in any environmental debate.
questions.explanation: "Der Klimawandel" means climate change — the central concept in any environmental debate in German.

questions.opener: A key word that differs from, but is easily confused with, "erneuerbar".
questions.explanation: "Nachhaltig" means sustainable (e.g. nachhaltige Entwicklung = sustainable development). The word is often confused with "erneuerbar" (renewable), which refers specifically to energy sources that renew naturally, such as sun and wind.

questions.opener: Look for the word that specifically refers to energy sources like sun, wind, and water.
questions.explanation: "Erneuerbare Energien" means renewable energy sources (sun, wind, water). "Fossile Brennstoffe" is the opposite (fossil fuels like coal and oil), and "der CO2-Ausstoß" means CO2 emissions.

questions.prompt:
Read: "Deutschland hat sich zum Ziel gesetzt, bis 2045 klimaneutral zu werden. Kritiker bezweifeln jedoch, dass dieses Ziel ohne einen deutlich schnelleren Ausbau der erneuerbaren Energien erreichbar ist."

What is Germany's goal, according to the text?
questions.opener: Look for the year and the word "klimaneutral".
choices: To phase out nuclear power by 2030
To become the world leader in solar power
questions.explanation: "Deutschland hat sich zum Ziel gesetzt, bis 2045 klimaneutral zu werden" means that Germany has set the goal of becoming climate-neutral by 2045.

questions.prompt: Same text. What do the critics (Kritiker) doubt?
questions.opener: "Bezweifeln" means to doubt — what follows that word in the sentence?
choices: That the goal is achievable without a significantly faster expansion of renewable energy
That climate change exists at all
That Germany has enough money for climate action
That other countries will follow Germany's example
questions.explanation: The text says the critics "bezweifeln, dass dieses Ziel ohne einen deutlich schnelleren Ausbau der erneuerbaren Energien erreichbar ist" — that is, that the goal cannot be reached without a significantly faster expansion of renewable energy.

questions.prompt: What does the verb "reduzieren" mean in the phrase "den CO2-Ausstoß reduzieren"?
questions.opener: A common verb in the climate debate that resembles an English word.
questions.explanation: "Reduzieren" means to reduce — "den CO2-Ausstoß reduzieren" means to reduce CO2 emissions. The word resembles the English "reduce", which makes it easy to recognize.

questions.prompt: Correct the error: "Um den Klimawandel zu bekämpfen, die Länder müssen erneuerbare Energien fördern." (Intended: In order to fight climate change, countries must promote renewable energy.)
questions.opener: An "um...zu" phrase counts as a single sentence element in the first position — what should happen to the verb right after it?
questions.answer: Um den Klimawandel zu bekämpfen, müssen die Länder erneuerbare Energien fördern.
steps: "Um den Klimawandel zu bekämpfen" is an infinitive phrase that functions as a single sentence element and occupies the first position of the sentence.
Since the main clause's conjugated verb must always stand in the second position, "müssen" needs to come directly after the comma — not the subject "die Länder".
Incorrect order: "..., die Länder müssen ..." (subject before verb) → correct: "..., müssen die Länder ..." (verb before subject).
Correct sentence: "Um den Klimawandel zu bekämpfen, müssen die Länder erneuerbare Energien fördern." The same rule applies whenever something other than the subject opens the sentence.

questions.prompt: What words and phrases do you need to discuss climate and the environment in German?
questions.opener: A vocabulary list for a social debate about Umwelt.
questions.answer: der Klimawandel = climate change. die Erderwärmung = global warming. nachhaltig = sustainable. erneuerbare Energien = renewable energy. fossile Brennstoffe = fossil fuels. der CO2-Ausstoß = CO2 emissions. reduzieren = to reduce. der Ausbau = the expansion. bekämpfen = to fight, combat. klimaneutral = climate-neutral. die Umweltschutzorganisation = the environmental protection organization. sich zum Ziel setzen = to set as a goal. bezweifeln = to doubt. Useful phrases: "Meiner Meinung nach müsste man ..." (In my opinion, one should ...), "Es ist wichtig, dass ..." (It is important that ...), "Einerseits ..., andererseits ..." (On the one hand ..., on the other hand ...).

questions.prompt: What does "der Ausbau" mean, as in "der Ausbau der erneuerbaren Energien"?
questions.opener: The word comes from the verb "ausbauen" (to expand).
questions.explanation: "Der Ausbau" means "the expansion", e.g. of renewable energy.

questions.prompt:
Read the sentence: "Viele Städte investieren derzeit in den Ausbau des öffentlichen Nahverkehrs, um den CO2-Ausstoß zu senken."

What does the sentence mean?
choices: Many cities are currently investing in expanding public transport to reduce CO2 emissions
Many cities have stopped investing in public transport
Many cities are building more highways
Many cities are banning public transport
questions.explanation: "Viele Städte investieren derzeit in den Ausbau des öffentlichen Nahverkehrs, um den CO2-Ausstoß zu senken" means "many cities are currently investing in expanding public transport to reduce CO2 emissions".

questions.prompt: What does the phrase "sich zum Ziel setzen" mean?
choices: To set something as a goal
questions.explanation: "Sich zum Ziel setzen" means "to set something as a goal", e.g. "Deutschland hat sich zum Ziel gesetzt, klimaneutral zu werden."

questions.opener: A common verb in the climate debate, combining "be-" and "Kampf" (fight).
questions.explanation: "Bekämpfen" means "to fight/combat", e.g. "den Klimawandel bekämpfen" (to fight climate change).

questions.prompt: What does the construction "Einerseits ..., andererseits ..." mean?
questions.opener: Used to weigh two sides of an issue against each other.
choices: On the one hand..., on the other hand...
questions.explanation: "Einerseits ..., andererseits ..." means "on the one hand ..., on the other hand ..." and is used to present two opposing aspects of the same issue.
